svg.text: Flow of control: web server, Controller (plain old object), InputBoundary,
Dependencies: all cross the boundaries pointing inward; adapters implement the
flow of control starts in the controller, passes through the use case and ends in
the presenter; source dependencies all point inward to the use case: invert with
DIP: the use case calls the OutputBoundary (use case output port) interface in the
inner circle and the presenter implements it
simple isolated structures (structs, DTOs, arguments, hashmaps), never Entity
objects or database row structures: always in the form most convenient for the
inner circle, so no inner circle learns an outer circle's format
Presenter and View: OutputData from the Interactor becomes a ViewModel of mostly Strings and flags (dates and currency already formatted, button and menu names, grey-
out flags); the View just moves it into the HTML page. Following the layers and the Dependency Rule makes the system intrinsically testable and lets obsolete externals
such as the database or web framework be replaced with minimum fuss.
